evals.name: new-endpoint-cost-per-repo
evals.prompt: i need a new endpoint on the api that gives me review cost per repo for the last 30 days — total spend and a breakdown by agent. there's a runs table with cost columns already i think. can you scaffold it out in server/? don't need it wired to the UI yet, just the backend bit.
evals.expected_output: A new slice under server/src/modules/ with routes.ts (schema only, thin handler), service.ts, repository.ts holding every Drizzle query, a Zod contract added to server/src/vendor/shared/contracts/ and mirrored to client/src/vendor/shared/, registration in modules/index.ts, and no drizzle-orm import in routes.ts or service.ts.
assertions: Creates a repository file that is the only place importing drizzle-orm or db/schema
routes.ts contains no drizzle-orm or db/schema import
service.ts contains no drizzle-orm, fastify, req or reply reference
Declares the request/response contract with Zod in the route schema rather than calling .parse() in the handler body
Places the shared contract in server/src/vendor/shared and mentions mirroring it to client/src/vendor/shared
Registers the new module in server/src/modules/index.ts
Uses ESM .js import specifiers
Adds no inline code comments to the new files
Does not introduce a top-level domain/, application/ or infrastructure/ folder

evals.name: refactor-fat-route
evals.prompt: server/src/modules/pulls/routes.ts has gotten out of hand — it's like 400 lines and does database queries and a github sync loop right inside the handlers. clean it up please
evals.expected_output: An extraction that follows the documented order: repository.ts first with the queries moved verbatim and workspaceId scoping preserved, then service.ts taking the repository, then the sync decisions named as domain rules. Handler reduced to parse -> one service call -> status. Behaviour unchanged.
assertions: Extracts a repository.ts containing the Drizzle queries before extracting a service
Preserves the existing workspaceId tenancy scoping on every query
Leaves routes.ts with no drizzle-orm or db/schema import
Moves the GitHub sync loop out of the handler into a service or use case
Does not change the HTTP contract or response shapes
References the migration guidance rather than inventing a different structure
Does not attempt to refactor the other three fat-route modules in the same pass

evals.name: placement-question-retry-rule
evals.prompt: quick q — where should the logic live that decides whether a failed review run gets retried? right now it's inline in the reviews service. it needs to know how many attempts happened and how long ago the last one was
evals.expected_output: Answer: a pure function in modules/reviews/domain.ts taking a snapshot plus the current time, called from service.ts. Explains that time must be injected (a Clock port or a now parameter) rather than read via Date.now() inside the rule, so it is testable, and notes the second-caller argument since the job runner also retries.
assertions: Answers domain.ts (ring 1) rather than service, repository or route
Says the rule must be a pure function with no repository or framework import
Addresses how the current time reaches the rule — injected parameter or Clock port, not Date.now() inside the rule
Explains why, not just where
Does not propose creating a new top-level folder
Mentions that it becomes unit-testable without Postgres or Fastify

evals.name: atomic-delete-across-repositories
evals.prompt: i need to delete a review run and all the findings attached to it in one go — if the findings delete fails the run must not disappear either. findings and runs are handled by different repository files in the reviews module. what's the cleanest way to do this here?
evals.expected_output: A unit-of-work / transaction port declared in ports.ts exposing a callback that receives transaction-bound stores, implemented in ring 3 over db.transaction. The service orchestrates atomicity without importing any Drizzle type. Should NOT hand a Drizzle transaction object to the service as a parameter.
assertions: Keeps every Drizzle type out of service.ts - no PgTransaction or db handle in a use-case signature
Proposes a transaction abstraction owned by the consumer (a port/interface) rather than passing Drizzle's transaction object around
Puts the db.transaction call in ring 3, not in the service or the route
Acknowledges the objection that a repository taking a transaction parameter has lost its abstraction
Does not suggest two sequential deletes with manual compensation instead of a transaction

evals.name: cross-slice-import-request
evals.prompt: in server/src/modules/settings i need to show which agents are configured. i was just going to do `import { AgentsService } from '../agents/service.js'` and call listAgents() — that fine?
evals.expected_output: No. Should refuse the cross-slice import and offer the three legal routes: shared row types via db/rows.ts, the container-held agentsRepo, or promoting the contract to ring 0. Should explain the modular-monolith reason rather than just asserting a rule.
assertions: Answers no to the direct cross-slice import
Offers a concrete alternative that exists in this repo (db/rows.ts, container.agentsRepo, or a vendor/shared contract)
Explains why cross-slice imports are the problem, not just that they are banned
Does not propose creating a shared 'common' or 'utils' module as the fix
Notes that the boundary check would flag it

evals.name: unit-test-service-without-postgres
evals.prompt: can you write me a unit test for the stale-run reaping in the reviews service? i don't want it spinning up a postgres container, the whole suite is getting slow
evals.expected_output: Should identify that ReviewService currently takes Container and news up its own repository, so it cannot be tested in isolation as written; then either propose the constructor change first or write the test against an extracted pure rule plus a fake store. Should use a hand-written fake implementing a port, not vi.mock of the repository module.
assertions: Identifies that the current constructor(container: Container) shape is what blocks the test
Uses a hand-written fake implementing an interface rather than vi.mock of a repository module
Injects time (fixed clock or now parameter) rather than relying on real Date.now
Names the test as a fast unit test, not *.it.test.ts
Does not silently rewrite the test as an integration test with testcontainers
